question.worked_solution:
Note that plugging in $x=16$ gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ However, we can use L'Hopital's rule to find this limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{{x}^{2}-20x+64}{\sqrt{x}-4} & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{[{x}^{2}-20x+64]^{′}}{[\sqrt{x}-4]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 16}\frac{2x-20}{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})} \\  & =\frac{2(16)-20}{(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{16}})} \\  & =\frac{32-20}{(\frac{1}{2(4)})} \\  & =\frac{12}{(\frac{1}{8})} \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$
